request.spec:
A retired person can be unretired (a button on the row; PERSON_UNRETIRED name=<name> on=<the
sheet's today>; anyone not retired is refused with an error on the row). They are no longer retired
(retired no, no retired-from); the retirement is kept on the row as <from> to <the day unretired>, one line per past
retirement; and a claim dated after the from and before the to of a
past retirement is refused as a claim after a retirement is.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A retired person can be unretired (a button on the row; PERSON_UNRETIRED name=<name> on=<the
sheet's today>; anyone not retired is refused with an error on the row). They are no longer retired
(retired no, no retired-from); the retirement is kept on the row as <from> to <the day unretired>, one line per past
retirement; and a claim dated after the from and before the to of a
past retirement is refused as a claim after a retirement is.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Unretiring is in place, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**What it does**
- Each person's row now has an **Unretire** button (`person-unretire`). It only works for someone who is retired. For anyone else it is refused: the row shows its error (`person-error`) and nothing is saved or written to the audit file.
- After unretiring, the person shows retired "no" and an empty retired-from date. The old retirement stays on the row as a line like `2026-03-05 to 2026-03-12` (`person-retirement-line`), one line per past retirement, earliest first.
- The audit file gets `PERSON_UNRETIRED … name=<name> on=<the sheet's today>`. The changed totals are then announced the same way a retirement announces them.
- A claim dated after the start and before the end of a past retirement is refused, just as a claim dated after a current retirement is. A claim on either boundary day is accepted. The same check runs when a claim is added, edited, re-dated or moved to another person, because they all go through the existing retirement check.

**Where the changes are**
- **Stored data:** a new `person_retirement` table (migration `V70__person_retirement.sql`). I also added it to the tables in `SheetPasts`, so it is captured along with the rest of a sheet's rows.
- **Server:**
  - `Person` keeps its past retirements, through a new `RetirementSpan` class.
  - `PersonService.unretire` is a new method, reached through `POST /api/sheets/{id}/people/{personId}/unretire`.
  - Each person sent to the screen now includes their past retirements.
  - `SheetAudit` writes the new record.
  - The claim check in `ClaimService` now covers past retirements too.
- **Front end:** the button, the retirement lines and the unretire call are in `people.ts`; the `Retirement` type is in `claims.ts`.

The end-of-day records behind the as-of view (`DayEnds`) don't include past retirements. Those records only feed the totals, and past retirements don't change the totals, only which claims are allowed.
